transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello Doctor. I'm coming in today because I've been having episodes where I eat an unusually large amount of food all at once. It feels like I completely lose control during these times and just can't stop myself from eating.
After these episodes of overeating, do you engage in any behaviors to prevent weight gain, such as self-induced vomiting, excessive exercise, or the misuse of laxatives?
No, I don't do anything like that to try and prevent weight gain. I've never forced myself to throw up, used laxatives, or exercised excessively after these episodes.
How often do these episodes of overeating typically occur, and do you find yourself eating much more rapidly than normal or eating until you feel uncomfortably full during these times?

These episodes usually happen about once a week, and this has been going on for about a year and two months now. I don't really think I eat faster than normal or until I'm uncomfortably full, though—I'm not really sure about those.
Do you feel significantly distressed, guilty, or ashamed about these eating episodes after they occur?
Yes, absolutely. I feel incredibly guilty and disgusted with myself every single time it happens. It really gets me down and leaves me feeling quite depressed afterward.
Do you often find that you eat these large amounts of food when you are not physically hungry, or do you tend to eat alone because you are embarrassed by how much you are eating?

I'm not entirely sure about the physical hunger part, to be honest. But I definitely tend to eat alone because I feel so embarrassed by the massive amount of food I'm consuming. I just don't want anyone else to see me like that.
During these episodes, do you find that you eat until you feel uncomfortably full, even when you aren't physically hungry?
I'm really not sure about that, to be honest. I haven't paid close enough attention to notice if I'm actually uncomfortably full or whether I was hungry before I started.
When you have these episodes, do you feel that your eating is out of control, or that you are unable to stop or limit what you are eating?
Yes, absolutely. Once I start eating, I feel a complete lack of control and it feels like I just can't stop myself. I feel totally unable to limit how much I'm consuming during those moments.

Beyond the feelings of guilt after eating, have you been experiencing other symptoms like persistent low mood, loss of interest in activities, changes in sleep, or feelings of worthlessness for most of the day, nearly every day?
No, I don't really experience those kinds of persistent symptoms throughout the day. I only feel that deep sadness, guilt, and low mood right after I have one of my overeating episodes.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Binge-Eating Disorder, Major Depressive Disorder]. Based on the patient's report that their low mood, feelings of worthlessness, and guilt are exclusively tied to the overeating episodes and are not persistent symptoms occurring for most of the day, nearly every day, Major Depressive Disorder is unlikely. The symptoms reported—recurrent episodes of eating large amounts of food with a sense of loss of control, occurring at least once a week for over a year, accompanied by significant distress and eating alone due to embarrassment—strongly align with Binge-Eating Disorder.
